subject.title: fix #95279: Provide a trusted inbound-decoration contract so consumers can strip/dedup without forgeable text heuristics

question: Should OpenClaw make trusted inbound-decoration state a permanent serialized contract, and if so should it live in an explicitly OpenClaw-owned metadata boundary rather than generic top-level message fields?
rationale: The mechanical fallback repair is clear, but choosing the permanent ownership and compatibility boundary for serialized trust metadata affects future producers, plugins, imports, and transcript readers.

options.title: Adopt an OpenClaw-owned contract
options.body: Keep the additive trusted-body behavior, place it behind an explicitly OpenClaw-owned metadata boundary, and require producers to set it only from canonical inbound data.

options.title: Keep top-level fields with a documented contract
options.body: Retain the proposed top-level fields but document their trusted-producer rules and add compatibility coverage for imports, hooks, and persisted transcripts.

options.title: Defer the serialized contract
options.body: Keep legacy stripping while a narrower design is agreed for trusted inbound metadata ownership.

recommendation.title: Adopt an OpenClaw-owned contract
recommendation.body: Keep the additive trusted-body behavior, place it behind an explicitly OpenClaw-owned metadata boundary, and require producers to set it only from canonical inbound data.

likelyOwner.reason: The canonical report defines the problem and proposed trust boundary; repository history ownership could not be independently verified in this read-only environment.
